07 / TRUST & COVERAGE

The records behind the view

SQL SERVER → AGGREGATED EXPORTS

source records were profiled across 48 original Parquet files. Trip-level originals remain intact; this dashboard contains compact SQL reporting aggregates.

Only pickup timestamps in 2024 enter the charts. Counts retain records with questionable duration, distance or fare; each metric uses its own eligible denominator. Unavailable fields remain unavailable.

Metric definitions and scope

Duration: dropoff minus pickup, greater than zero and no more than four hours. Source timestamps are timezone-naive NYC local clock values; no UTC conversion or DST correction is inferred.

Distance: reported miles greater than zero and at most 200. FHV does not report distance. Speed screening: valid duration/distance pairs implying more than 100 mph are flagged for review. The dashboard does not present mixed-route speed as a congestion or service-performance KPI.

Fares: Yellow/Green metered fare and high-volume base passenger fare use different definitions. No combined fare total is shown. Nonnegative base-fare values up to $1,000 are included in service-specific averages. FHV fares are unavailable.

Quality: flags are overlapping and are shown for the selected source-file partition month and service. Distance, speed and fare quality percentages exclude FHV from the source-row denominator because it does not report those fields. Screening limits are analytical choices, not proof of erroneous records. Batch-level matching of selected fields is not shown as a duplicate-trip metric; all source records are retained. No person or vehicle identity is inferred.

Source populations: TLC publishes Yellow, Green, FHV and high-volume FHV separately. Recorded submissions do not establish every actual trip or transport market share. “All services” combines these published records without treating ordinary FHV as a parent of high-volume FHV.
